entities.name: Bacterial meningitis
observations: CSF profile in a 21-day-old infant is strongly consistent with acute bacterial meningitis: neutrophilic pleocytosis, low glucose, elevated protein, and elevated opening pressure.

entities.name: Ampicillin
observations: Empiric neonatal meningitis component covering Group B Streptococcus and Listeria monocytogenes.

entities.name: Cefotaxime
observations: Empiric neonatal meningitis component providing CNS-penetrating coverage for E. coli and other enteric gram-negative bacilli; preferred over gentamicin when meningitis is suspected because of better CSF penetration.

entities.name: Acyclovir
observations: Not routinely required when CSF and clinical findings strongly suggest bacterial meningitis and there are no compelling HSV features, though HSV testing and a low threshold for treatment remain appropriate.

entities.name: Ceftriaxone
observations: Generally avoided in neonates because of bilirubin displacement and calcium-related safety concerns.

entities.name: Neonatal meningitis regimen
observations: For a previously healthy 21-day-old with bacterial meningitis, the core empiric regimen is IV ampicillin plus IV cefotaxime; among the listed options, D contains both core agents, while gentamicin is an additional neonatal-sepsis component.

entities.name: PMID:25425552
observations: 2015 European Journal of Cardio-Thoracic Surgery report titled “First registry results from the newly approved ACURATE TA TAVI system.”
Post-market multicentre registry included the first 250 CE-mark-approved ACURATE TA implants across 17 sites in Germany, Italy, Switzerland, and Argentina.
Patients were high-risk elderly; procedural success was 98%, 30-day mortality 6.8%, stroke 2.8%, moderate paravalvular leak 2.3%, and new pacemaker implantation 10.0%.
Authors concluded short-term safety and efficacy were comparable with, or improved versus, previously approved TAVI devices, with favorable functional outcomes.

entities.name: ACURATE TA TAVI
observations: Self-expanding nitinol transapical transcatheter aortic valve system developed by Symetis; the registry report evaluated its initial post-CE-mark real-world use.

entities.name: ACURATE TA first registry
observations: The exact phrase “First registry results from the newly approved ACURATE TA TAVI system” is the title of PMID:25425552, confirming that this is the requested first registry report.

The initial 250-patient real-world registry showed 98% procedural success and low rates of moderate paravalvular leak (2.3%) and stroke (2.8%), but 6.8% 30-day mortality in a high-risk elderly population.
